name: Real-time clock RV-3028 breakout (19 x 19 x 4 mm, 45 nA)
description: Extreme-low-power real-time clock: Micro Crystal RV-3028-C7 on Pimoroni's 19 x 19 x 4 mm breakout with a tiny 337 backup cell, I2C at 0x52. The chip draws 45 nA (the DS3231 0.11 mA, a ZS-042 with its LED about 2 mA), so it is the clock for thin battery devices that sleep for weeks. Wire 2-6V → 3V3, SDA → SDA, SCL → SCL, GND → GND (INT optional). It is not an RTClib chip: read registers 0x00-0x06 (BCD) with Wire, or the UNIX counter at 0x1B-0x1E. It ships with the backup switchover off: enable it once (EEPROM 0x37 BSM = 11) or the cell keeps nothing.

pins.label: 2-6V
pins.description: Supply (I2C works from 1.2 V at 100 kHz, 2 V at 400 kHz; 5.5 V max).

pins.label: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output (open drain, active low): alarm, timer, update. Not modelled: stays high-impedance.

props.label: Time at t = 0
props.description: Clock time when the simulation starts. A scenario's clock and set_clock set it too; the sketch can write the time registers.

props.label: Power-on reset flag
props.description: Start with PORF (status 0x0E bit 0) set, as after the chip lost all power and the time is wrong.

footprint: 19 x 19 mm breakout, 5-pin 0.1 in header (Breakout Garden / Pi pins 1-9 order), 337 silver-oxide cell on board
